svg.title: “Ozempic vagina” and “Ozempic vulva”: what the evidence shows
svg.desc: “Ozempic vagina” and “Ozempic vulva”: what the evidence shows. “Ozempic makes the vagina fall out” (prolapse): No study found: 0 PubMed records for GLP-1 drugs and pelvic organ prolapse. Verdict: No evidence. Weight loss and prolapse symptoms (PRIDE trial): Diet-and-exercise weight loss did not improve bothersome prolapse symptoms. Verdict: No change. Weight loss and bladder leaks (PRIDE, Look AHEAD): Fewer leaks and fewer new cases with 5-10% weight loss; not drug trials. Verdict: Better. “Ozempic vulva” (fat loss in labia majora, mons): Described by surgeons and clinicians; a weight-loss effect, not a diagnosis. Verdict: Plausible. Coded vulvar atrophy or hypertrophy (2026 abstract): 617,407 GLP-1 users: 0.061% vs 0.060% in non-users; misses cosmetic change. Verdict: No rise found. Low desire, dryness, orgasm problems: Case reports and reviews; FDA reports not significant; few data in women. Verdict: Unsettled. Wegovy and Zepbound labels: No vulvar, vaginal, pelvic-floor or sexual adverse reactions listed. Verdict: Not listed. Trials measuring pelvic floor on GLP-1 drugs: One 200-woman observational study registered, not yet recruiting. Verdict: Not yet done.
